newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian bonds open stronger after U.S. PPI data.
newsitem.headline: Canadian bonds open stronger after U.S. PPI data.

text.p: Canadian bonds opened stronger for a fourth consecutive session on Friday, boosted by the release of a report showing U.S. producer prices were subdued in May, analysts said.
"It's building on the gains of the last few days entirely on the U.S. data," said Harv Kalirai, Canadian analyst with financial analysis firm I.D.E.A. "It's reducing scope for Fed hike fears."
Canada's 30-year benchmark rose C$0.81 to C$116.75 to yield 6.697 percent
The U.S. 30-year bond rose 15/32 to yield 6.74 percent. The negative spread between the bonds widened to four basis points from two basis points on Thursday.
The Canada-U.S. 30-year spread on Thursday began trading negative for the first time in history.

Both Canadian and U.S. fixed-income markets strengthened after the U.S. Labor Department reported on Friday that the producer price index fell 0.3 percent in May, compared with expectations of a 0.1 percent rise. The report decreased expectations that the U.S. Federal Reserve will hike rates in July.

"I think it just buys the Bank of Canada time (to hold rates steady). Their focus is on the output gap, and the longer the Fed delays action the more time the Bank of Canada has to let the economy grow above trend to close the output gap," said Kalirai.

Expectations that the Fed will hold rates steady in the near term also benefitted the Canadian dollar. The currency had been under pressure from expectations a near-term Fed hike would draw capital flows out of Canada.
In other prices, Canada's 10-year benchmark bond rose C$0.51 to C$108.13 to yield 6.139 percent while the U.S. 10-year rose 12/32 to 6.44 percent.
The negative spread between the bonds widened to 30 basis points from 27 basis points at Thursday's close.
The three-month cash T-bill yielded 2.85 percent against its U.S. equivalent which yielded 4.95 percent.
